facts.text: San Miguel was officially founded on August 10, 1896, marking its transition from rural land to an urban commune.
The commune’s name honors Saint Michael the Archangel, stemming from a 1575 hermitage built by Gaspar Banda.
Bernardo O'Higgins, Chile’s liberator, once owned the land that became San Miguel and used it as a vacation home.
In the late 19th century, Ramón Subercaseaux imported Bordeaux wine strains, earning San Miguel wines international acclaim at Paris 1889 Exposition.
At the start of the 20th century, San Miguel adopted a European garden‑city layout, featuring large mansions, parks, and tree‑lined streets.
The civic square in front of the city hall hosts a statue of José Miguel Carrera, sculpted by Auguste Dumont, the same artist who carved Napoleon’s statue in Paris.
